issues.legal_issue: Prior central approval is not required to extract additional minerals from forest land already disturbed for mining before the restriction took effect, provided the extraction does not expand the disturbed area or involve unapproved tree removal.
material_facts: A mining lease granted before the restriction took effect authorized mining for one mineral.
Mining had already broken up and disturbed a limited part of the leased forest area before the restriction took effect.
During existing mining operations, the lessee discovered additional minerals and the lease was amended to permit their extraction.
The lessee undertook to confine operations to the area already used for mining and not to remove standing trees without prior written approval.
issues.conclusion: The lessee could extract the additional minerals from the previously disturbed area without prior central approval, subject to the undertaking not to expand operations or remove standing trees without prior written approval; the appeal was disposed of with the High Court judgment affirmed as modified.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(ii) of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, read with its Explanation, requires prior Central Government approval for fresh breaking up or clearing of forest land for a non-forest purpose. It does not require such approval for mining in forest land already broken up or cleared before the Act came into force. The Court reasoned that requiring approval merely to extract additional minerals encountered during existing operations would produce an unreasonable result that would not further the Act’s object. No earlier cases are relied upon.

rule.if: mining_permission_appeal and lease_predates_restriction and land_disturbed_for_mining_before_restriction and additional_minerals_found_during_existing_operations and extraction_confined_to_previously_disturbed_area and operator_commits_to_avoid_unapproved_tree_removal

predicates.mining_permission_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether mining permission may be exercised in forest land.
predicates.lease_predates_restriction: The mining lease was granted before the restriction took effect.
predicates.land_disturbed_for_mining_before_restric: The forest land used for the proposed mining had already been broken up for mining before the restriction took effect.
predicates.additional_minerals_found_during_existin: The lessee found additional minerals while carrying out mining operations authorized by the existing lease.
predicates.extraction_confined_to_previously_distur: The lessee undertook to extract the additional minerals only from the area already disturbed for mining.
predicates.operator_commits_to_avoid_unapproved_tre: The lessee undertook not to remove standing trees without prior written approval.
predicates.prior_central_approval_not_required_for_: Prior central approval is not required to extract additional minerals from the previously disturbed mining area.

issues.definition: When a mining-permission appeal concerns a pre-existing lease, additional minerals found during existing operations, land already disturbed before the restriction, extraction confined to that land, and a commitment to avoid unapproved tree removal, prior central approval is not required for the additional mineral extraction.
